issues.description: Stock clearing method name is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement UML declares Stock.emptyStock(): void (problem_statement.md line 54) and the solution implementation defines public void emptyStock() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java, but the template implementation defines the method as public void clearInventory() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java. This identifier mismatch (emptyStock vs clearInventory) can confuse students who will follow the UML/spec and the solution examples and then not find the expected method in the template, leading to compilation/runtime mismatches or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across all artifacts. Either: (A) Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (public void emptyStock()) so the template, UML/problem statement, and solution use the same name; or (B) Update the problem statement UML and the solution to use clearInventory() instead. Ensure any tests or example code are updated to call the chosen method name and keep the signature public void <name>().
